name: Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) Pilot Program
description: Incentives to offset the cost of a two-way charger that powers your home from your EV battery, plus ongoing earnings for supporting the grid
fullDescription: PG&E's V2X program provides incentives to help offset the extra cost of bidirectional EV chargers that can power your home using your electric vehicle's battery during outages or send power back to the grid.
whatTheyOffer:
- Upfront incentive toward a bidirectional charger (about $2,500 for homes, $3,000 in disadvantaged communities)
- Early adopter bonus and additional state grant funding may be available for eligible customers
- Powers home from EV battery during outages
- Additional earnings through performance-based incentives and the Emergency Load Reduction Program
- Growing list of eligible vehicles and chargers (Ford, GM, Tesla, Kia, Volvo, Nissan and more added in 2026)
howToGetIt:
1. Must be a PG&E residential or commercial customer (some CCA customers also qualify)
2. Own an EV and bidirectional charger combination on PG&E's Eligible Product Lists
3. Hire an EVITP-certified electrician for installation
4. Get a Rule 21 interconnection agreement for grid-connected systems; be on a time-of-use rate for Hourly Flex Pricing
5. Enroll through PG&E's V2X program page before June 30, 2027
keywords: V2X, bidirectional charger, EV, Ford F-150 Lightning, PG&E, backup power, home battery, vehicle to grid
